comparator.name: Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define a mandatory 150-EC Physics major and a 30-EC free minor. The pathway below accounts for the complete 180 EC. Wherever the major requires a restricted choice, the first-listed option is used as the neutral official-order tie-break: Introduction to Astronomy in Year 1, Biomaterials 1 in Year 2, and Nanophysics and Nanotechnology plus Advanced Electrodynamics in Year 3. The genuine 30-EC minor remains open rather than being populated with an invented specialization. No formal route is defined. The live programme page and adopted regulations were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled route and 180-EC reconstruction remain unchanged.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the mathematical Earth-and-energy route, thirteen courses (97.5 EC) change in each direction. progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in Year 1 and eight 300-level courses. alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. The closest route responds to mathematical modelling and energy/environmental applications; the second is a genuinely different biomedical-systems and imaging route, with thirteen courses / 97.5 EC unique to each. A third fundamental or experimental Physics route is not feasible because UCR lacks mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, particle, nuclear and nano physics and a cumulative experimental-physics laboratory sequence. Physics education is separately rejected because the workbook lacks both the required Physics subject preparation and Physics didactics; professional qualification alone is not the basis for rejection.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide programming and computational problem-solving; UCR supplies general Python foundations rather than physics-specific computation.
Both establish calculus and differential-equation tools, while the Groningen course is embedded in a disciplinary Physics sequence.
Both directly study matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations.
Both develop numerical methods for equations, integration and differential equations; UCR is not a computational-physics laboratory.
Both extend calculus; UCR covers multivariable calculus, complex functions and differential equations without the surrounding physics sequence.
Linear Systems directly studies differential equations, signals and system responses, but not the mechanics or field theory built around them in Physics.

notes.text: Groningen Physics provides a cumulative disciplinary sequence in mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, atomic, solid-state and subatomic physics, advanced physics laboratories and a Physics research project. UCR can build coherent related programmes in mathematical modelling, Earth and energy systems, or biomedical systems and imaging, but these do not reproduce a Physics degree.

UCR offers substantial mathematics, programming, data science, Earth science, sustainability and life science. It lacks the comparator’s dedicated Physics theory sequence, instrumentation and experimental-physics laboratories, particle and nano physics, and compulsory 15-EC Physics research project.
